e.etymology: A respelling of Lainey, a pet form of Elaine, the Old French form of Helen, and of Delaney. Country star Lainey Wilson has lifted every spelling of the name since 2022.
A Spanish name used mainly in Mexico, probably a variant of Isabel or Isabella. It also echoes Gisela and Marisela.
A spelling of Stormy, the English word used as a given name in the United States since the mid-1900s. Stormi, with an i, is the spelling Kylie Jenner chose for her daughter in 2018.

assoc.t: Stormy Daniels, adult film star (same sound)
Stormi Webster, Kylie Jenner's daughter (same sound)

e.etymology: A respelling of Adalynn, a modern American elaboration of Ada and Adeline with the -lynn ending. Those names go back to Germanic adal, 'noble'.

e.meaning: alif, the first letter; slender and upright
e.etymology: From Arabic alif, the first letter of the alphabet, by way of Ottoman Turkish. The letter is a single upright stroke, so the name is taken to mean 'slender, upright'. It is a top girls' name in Turkey.
From Latin Constantinus, from constans, 'constant, steadfast'. Constantine the Great, the first Christian Roman emperor, made it a lasting favorite in the Orthodox world.
namesakes: Constantine the Great (first Christian Roman emperor)
John Constantine (DC Comics occult detective, played by Keanu Reeves)

assoc.t: Constantine the Great, first Christian Roman emperor
John Constantine, DC Comics occult detective

e.etymology: A French pet form of Marie, made with the ending -elle. Marie is the French form of Mary, from Hebrew Miryam.

From the biblical city and region of Samaria, capital of the northern kingdom of Israel, in Hebrew Shomron. The Bible says King Omri named it for Shemer, who sold him the hill; the root means 'to watch, guard'.

assoc.t: Samaria, biblical region of the Good Samaritan

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that puts an A- on Nylah, in the family of Aniyah and Anaya.
In Albanian luan is the word for 'lion'. Luan is also a popular Brazilian name of debated origin, and a Vietnamese name written with characters meaning 'ethics' or 'discourse'.
A K spelling of Carmelo, the Italian and Spanish masculine of Carmel, from Hebrew karmel, 'garden, orchard', the name of Mount Carmel in Israel.

assoc.t: Carmelo Anthony, NBA star known as Melo (same sound)

e.etymology: From Arabic 'inaya, 'care, concern, protection', often understood as God's care for a person. It is popular among Muslim families in South Asia and the West.
A transliteration of Russian Natalya, from Latin Natalia, based on natale domini, 'the birthday of the Lord', that is, Christmas. Natasha is its Russian pet form.
A short form of Emily, Emma and Emmeline, usually said like Emmy. It rose after Jennifer Lopez and Marc Anthony chose it for their daughter in 2008.
A modern name that appears to join Jah, the short form of the Hebrew name of God used in Rastafari, with Zara. The often-repeated gloss 'blessed princess' in Amharic has no reliable source.
From Greek theia, 'goddess, divine'. Theia was the Titaness of sight and shining light, mother of the sun (Helios), the moon (Selene) and the dawn (Eos).

assoc.t: Theia, hypothesized planet whose impact formed the Moon

e.etymology: From the aster, a daisy-like flower whose name is the Latin and Greek word for star. Aster is also the Ethiopian form of Esther.

assoc.t: aster, the daisy-like fall garden flower

e.etymology: An English surname of unexplained origin, possibly a variant of Higgins. As a first name it is recent and American, known from Tim Riggins of Friday Night Lights.
namesakes: Tim Riggins (brooding fullback on Friday Night Lights)
John Riggins (Hall of Fame Washington running back)

assoc.t: Tim Riggins of TV's Friday Night Lights

e.etymology: A Latin American name, an extended form of Yamile and Yamila, which are Spanish spellings of Arabic Jamila, beautiful.

e.meaning: combination of Anna (grace) and Beth (God is my oath)
e.etymology: A combination of Anna and Beth, both Hebrew in origin. It is best known from Annabeth Chase, the heroine of the Percy Jackson books, and from actress Annabeth Gish.
namesakes: Annabeth Chase (heroine of the Percy Jackson books)
Annabeth Gish (actress in Mystic Pizza and The X-Files)

assoc.t: Annabeth Chase of the Percy Jackson series

e.etymology: Two separate names share the spelling. The Indian boys' name is Sanskrit samara, battle. The Arabic name, given mostly to girls, means evening conversation, the talk shared after dark.

assoc.t: Samar, large island in the Philippines

e.etymology: A modern American name, apparently Damon lengthened with the -i ending of Armani and Imani. Damon is Greek, from a verb meaning to tame.
A spelling of Elsie, the Scottish pet form of Elizabeth by way of Elspeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath. Spanish speakers borrowed it from English in this spelling.
Japanese kaori is the everyday word for fragrance. As a name it is written in kana or with kanji such as those for fragrance and weaving.
The Greek spelling of Calliope, from kallos, beauty, and ops, voice. Kalliope was the foremost of the nine Muses, the one who inspired epic poetry.

assoc.t: Calliope, Muse of epic poetry in Greek myth
calliope, the steam-whistle organ of circuses and riverboats

e.etymology: A K spelling of Cassius, a Roman family name of uncertain meaning, sometimes linked to Latin cassus, hollow. Cassius Clay was the birth name of Muhammad Ali.
A spelling of Skyla, a modern name built on sky or shortened from Skylar, which comes from the Dutch surname Schuyler, scholar.

assoc.t: Skyla, a hormonal IUD brand (spelled Skyla)

e.etymology: A spelling of Ethan, from Hebrew Eitan, firm or enduring. Ethan the Ezrahite is a wise man named in the Old Testament.
A modern American name built on oak, a variant of Oaklyn and Oakland.
A short form of Donald, from Gaelic Domhnall, world ruler. Don is also the Spanish and Italian title of respect for a man, as in Don Quixote.
namesakes: Don Draper (the ad man of Mad Men)
Don Henley (singer and drummer of the Eagles)

assoc.t: a don, a Mafia boss, as in The Godfather
Don, Spanish and Italian title of respect

e.etymology: A pet form of Reginald, the Latinized form of a Germanic name built from words for counsel and rule. It is also short for Regina, Latin for queen.
namesakes: Reggie Jackson (Hall of Fame slugger known as Mr. October)
Reggie Miller (Indiana Pacers Hall of Fame shooter)

assoc.t: Reggie Mantle of Archie Comics and Riverdale

e.etymology: A spelling of Annabella, the Latinate form of Annabel, a medieval Scottish name thought to be an altered form of Amabel, from Latin amabilis, lovable.
